item: A CHECKPOINT before every shard's aggregate lets the in-memory rollup build reach 28 M mentions at 1,004 MB (R169), and a plain out-of-memory error is named at its stage
summary: The in-memory rollup stays in uncompressed write buffers until something checkpoints it, so the rollup alone was hundreds of MiB by the last shards. columnar._checkpoint now runs before each shard's aggregate (same classification as the final compact: an allocation FatalException is a duckdb-limit stop at stage checkpoint with the shard, any other fatal is the unusable-instance failure, any other error carries on and is counted); plan_build_shards is unchanged. A plain OutOfMemoryException in a staged insert is the same wall: a type-only _PlainEngineWall turns it into a duckdb-limit stop at stage-insert or keywords with engine_error_class OutOfMemoryException (before, a raw error and a stage-less skip); interrupts still propagate raw and no engine text is kept. MEASURED (DuckDB 1.5.6, memory_limit 1,004 MB, no offload, 2 threads, 16 GB machine, poller-free, seeded corpora of 8 mentions per keyword): the base build (a checkpoint only after the build) built 16 M (7 of 7), declined at 20 M (0 of 8, keywords-stage FATAL), raised a raw OutOfMemoryException at 24 M (2 of 2) and declined at the last shard at 28 M (2 of 2); with a checkpoint before every shard it built 20 M (5 of 5), 24 M (2 of 2) and 28 M (2 of 2). WHICH CODE: the keyword-machine 20, 24 and 28 M cells at 1,004 MB ran the bench's patched aggregate (it checkpoints first), not the shipped columnar._checkpoint; the shipped code itself was measured in Export's 28 M runs and in the 600 and 450 MB runs. Boundary reads / resident after the final compact (MiB): 16 M 199 / 81, 20 M 241 / 99, 24 M 280 / 121, 28 M 288 / 135. 28 M also BUILT at 600 MB (2 of 2) but the serve check (canary) passed in 1 of the 2 (the other read out-of-memory, which the app keeps as a duckdb-limit stop at stage serve-check and does not serve), and it was declined at 450 MB (2 of 2, stage keywords, OutOfMemoryException): the BUILD floor at 28 M lies between 450 and 600 MB, not narrowed further, and 600 MB is not shown to be above the SERVING floor. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by the Export lane on another machine (same generator, 28 M at 1,004 MB): boundary reads 288.1, resident after build 453.8, after compact 134.8 to 135.0 and every parity digest (per-term counts and ranked values, 7 d, 30 d, all) equal to the digit, and the base build declined at the same stage, shard and class (aggregate, shard 34, FatalException). DuckDB-accounted memory (duckdb_memory(), what memory_limit enforces) is the figure; process high-water is PER MACHINE and includes the interpreter: 691 to 695 MiB on the keyword machine (about 83 MiB baseline) against 738 to 779 on Export's (124 to 125 MiB measured baseline). OPEN: whether the real checkpoint adds about 23 MiB of process memory over the bench's patched aggregate (Export: 765 and 779 against 738 and 759, n=2 each, ranges do not overlap but the spread is the same size; not isolated; DuckDB's counters are identical). NO wall-clock claim (machine-dependent: Export's seconds were 40 to 50 percent shorter). Query parity (digests of the per-term counts and of the ranked top-80 values per window, not of the rollup's rows): base and per-shard-checkpoint identical at 16 M (4 runs). KNOWN LIMIT: the all-history top terms return 0 rows (the live scan answers, counted in serve_fallbacks) from 20 M mentions up and at 16 M with a 600 MB limit. NOT CLAIMED: any ceiling above 28 M; any other machine. THE 8 MACHINES OF THE 16 OCTOBER BUNDLES (28.9 to 33.4 M mentions, limit 738 MiB): #1427 attempts the build on them with no up-front decline (plan_build_shards returns fits=False at 35 to 38 shards and nothing reads it; BUILD_CODE_VERSION is bumped to 3 in this PR, so a stop kept by any earlier code is released on upgrade and the build is tried again); MEASURED HERE, NOT ON THEIR MACHINES (one machine, 16 GB, DuckDB 1.5.6, memory_limit 738 MB (the app's duckdb_limit_mb is decimal MB, so 704 MiB: the cells ran stricter than 738 MiB would be, and the 16 October bundles' 738 is the same field, which their findings call MiB), 2 threads, no offload, the planner's own shard count, the shipped per-shard checkpoint, poller-free, idle baseline 83 MiB; the corpus was EXTENDED IN PLACE from the 28 M one (rollup-bench-2026-10-17/extend_corpus.py DB 3500000 28000000 3625000 29000000, then DB 3625000 29000000 4175000 33400000; the mention counts are those arguments, not a field of the raw file), so the first 28 M mentions are the 28 M cell's rows, keywords were added to keep about 8 mentions each, and the new mentions fall uniformly over all keywords): 29 M mentions BUILT 1 of 1 (35 shards, resident 467.3 MiB after the build, 136.5 after the compact, high-water 713 MiB, serve check ok); 33.4 M mentions BUILT 2 of 2 (38 shards, 0 splits, boundary reads 361.3, resident 540.6 and 541.1 after the build, 160.8 and 161.5 after the compact, process high-water 783 and 785 MiB after the build and 801 after the compact, serve check ok in both). The all-history top terms return 0 rows there too. Their machines have 4.81 GiB and a different corpus shape, so this is a measurement of the build at their sizes, not a promise for them.
